name: kubernetes_ops
description: Execute Kubernetes operations via kubectl for cluster management, workload inspection, debugging, and remediation. Supports read-only queries (get, describe, logs, top, events), rollout management (rollout status, rollout restart, rollout undo), and supervised mutations (scale, apply, delete). All mutation operations require confirmation via the infrastructure_ops skill guardrails. Use `-o json` or `-o yaml` for structured output when parsing is needed.

parameters.name: command
parameters.description: kubectl command arguments. Examples: 'get pods -n production -o wide', 'describe deployment my-app -n staging', 'logs pod/my-app-xyz -n production --tail=100 --previous', 'top nodes', 'rollout status deployment/my-app -n production', 'get events -n production --sort-by=.lastTimestamp'. Do NOT include the 'kubectl' prefix — it is added automatically.

usage_guidance:
Use for ALL Kubernetes cluster operations. Before executing, consult the infrastructure_ops skill for routing and guardrail checks.

**Read-only commands** (autonomous — no confirmation needed):
  get, describe, logs, top, explain, api-resources, api-versions, cluster-info, config view, version, diff, events

**Low-risk mutations** (log and confirm via skill):
  scale, rollout restart, rollout undo, cordon, uncordon, label, annotate

**High-risk mutations** (require human approval):
  apply, patch, create, replace, set

**Blocked operations** (never execute — escalate to human):
  delete namespace, delete --all, drain, taint

Always specify namespace explicitly with -n <namespace> for namespaced resources. Prefer -o json for structured output when results will be parsed programmatically.
returns: Command output from kubectl. Text by default; structured JSON with -o json flag; YAML with -o yaml flag. Error output includes kubectl error messages and exit codes.
